title: Lyra retail prospect digest
body:
Quick brain dump on Lyra (mid-market omni-retailer) — raw notes for outreach + pilot sketched out. Keep it short, iterative, share with SEs before first call.

Context:
- Lyra is scaling personalization & conversational support across web + in-store tablets. They run inference on a mix of managed AWS endpoints and some on-prem infra for sensitive stores. Heard from intro call w/ Sofia: main goals are lower latency for chat widgets, reduce per-session cost for NLU reranking, and hardened private deployment for partner stores (PCI adjacent).
- Key contacts: Head of ML (Priya Rao), Platform Eng manager (Tom Becker), Head of Digital Ops (Ana Ruiz).

Why Redwood can win (elevator bullets):
- Consistent API across Hosted / Dedicated / Private — they like that they can start hosted and pin to private later.
- Predictable latency + autoscaling for bursts (dedicated pools + SLOs) — hit their performance bar for checkout assistant.
- Cost levers: batching, prefix caching, quantization suggestions from Redwood Optimize — measurable cost down from current per-token spend.
- Observability: per-route token breakdowns, eval-linked regressions, rollouts/canaries — appeals to platform team.

Key technical selling points to emphasize (for SE prep):
- Serving runtime: GPU-optimized kernels, KV cache behavior for chat sessions (reduces repeated prompt tokens), automatic fallback to smaller model when overloaded.
- Private: VPC-mode control plane + KMS integration, audit logs for store-level access — call out on-prem package if stores require air-gapped options.
- Model catalog: curated open models + performance profiles so they can compare latency/cost tradeoffs without heavy model ops work.

Pilot hypothesis (6-week sketch):
Goal: validate performance, cost, and rollout mechanics on a small traffic slice (5% of web chat sessions).
Success metrics: p95 latency < 250ms for generation (on dedicated pool), end-to-end error rate < 1%, 20-30% reduction in per-session inference cost vs current prod, integration time < 3 weeks for devs.
Scope & phases:
- Week 0: onboarding + infra scoping (account + IAM + certs), access to sample traffic/measurements.
- Week 1–2: test harness + model selection (hosted) — run perf matrix vs Lyra baselines.
- Week 3–4: dedicated pool config + KV/prefix caching experiments, tune batching.
- Week 5–6: canary routing (5% traffic), telemetry + cost report, rollback/auto-fallback drills.
Deliverables: perf report, cost delta calc, runbook for private migration, rollout guide.

Outbound sequence (first touch ideas) — short copy for Maya -> Priya/Tom:
Email subject options: "Proof: 30% inference cost drop for retail chat" / "Quick pilot to cut chat latency + cost at Lyra"
Cold email (concise):
Hi Priya — quick note from Maya at Redwood Inference. We help retailers run LLM inference with predictable latency and lower unit cost (dedicated GPU pools + automatic prefix caching). Could we scope a 6-week pilot to target p95 <250ms and ~20% cost reduction on your chat flow? 15 min to sync this week?
- CTA: 15-min sync + share current p95 tokens/traffic numbers.
LinkedIn opener (short):
Hi Priya — noticed Lyra is ramping in-store conversational experiences. I work on pilots at Redwood Inference (reducing latency/cost for retail ML). Quick 10-min intro?
Voicemail / call hooks:
- "We ran a 5% traffic canary for a retailer and cut per-session inference spend by 28% while keeping latency under 200ms — want to see the perf matrix?"

Common objections & quick counters (prep for AE/SE):
1) "We already run endpoints on AWS; why switch?"
- Counter: Redwood is not just another endpoint — it's a runtime + orchestration layer with built-in batching, KV caching, model variants, and deterministic fallbacks. You can start hosted and keep same API surface while we manage tail latency and cost optimization.
2) "Security/compliance worries (PCI, PII in-store)."
- Counter: Private deployment options (VPC + on-prem), KMS/HSM integration, audit logs. Offer an architecture walkthrough and SAML/KMS details.
3) "We’ve invested in model fine-tuning and custom weights."
- Counter: We support pinned versions and private model artifacts; runtime is model-agnostic and optimizes kernels/quantization to match your weights. Also offer canary rollouts to validate regressions.
4) "Operational lock-in concerns."
- Counter: Emphasize API compatibility and export path; tooling focuses on transparent perf/cost profiles and allows private deployment/export of models.

Technical questions to get early (what to ask on first tech call):
- Current per-session token distribution (avg tokens in prompt + completion).
- Typical sequence length and p95 latency targets.
- Traffic shape: QPS, burstiness, peak hours (store opening times).
- Existing infra: are there edge devices, on-prem proxies, store-level appliances?
- Compliance: data residency or log retention limits.

Notes for SEs:
- Bring perf matrix from similar retailers (anonymized) showing batching + caching gains.
- Prepare quick demo: hosted endpoint -> toggle KV caching -> show token drop & latency improvement.
- Have sample cost model template: input tokens/day -> estimate cost hosted vs dedicated vs private.

Next steps (short):
- Get intros: Maya to send 1-line intro to Priya & Tom w/ proposed 15-min slots (this week).
- Align SE: Evan to draft perf matrix + sample report by Mon 3/15.
- Legal: if Priya asks for security pack, pull security-and-compliance brief (product repo link in artifacts).

Open questions / risks:
- Lyra might insist on on-prem from day 1 for PCI-adjacent stores — need SRE time estimate for on-prem packaging (ask infra for rough sizing).
- Their fine-tuned models may rely on ops we haven’t validated at scale (LRU KV behavior with custom tokenizers) — include model onboarding checklist in pilot.

Scratch email draft (longer, if needed):
Subject: pilot idea: cut chat latency + cost (6-week, low-risk)
Hi Priya — enjoyed the product write-up. We’ve worked with several retailers to reduce inference unit economics while improving tail latency via model-aware serving (kernel selection, KV/prefix caching) + dedicated pools. I’d propose a 6-week scoped pilot focused on your web chat flow (5% traffic canary). We’ll deliver a perf/cost delta and a production-ready runbook for private migration. Can you share a 15-min slot this week?
—Maya

Keep this as staging doc — will refine before first outreach. Add SE notes inline once Evan posts the perf matrix.
